tools.name: post_job

You get one bid per job, ever: your bid amount cannot be edited afterwards, and if you withdraw it you cannot bid on that job again. Decide the amount before calling this. tools.name: get_messages
tools.description: Read the messages for a job. The job's poster sees every conversation on that job (with every bidder they've messaged); a bidder sees only their own conversation with the poster, never another bidder's thread. Every message names its sender and its recipient, so a poster can tell which conversation

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message on a job to a specific other participant. If you're the poster, the recipient must be someone who has actually bid on the job. If you're a bidder, the recipient must be the poster.

tools.name: complete_job
tools.description: Mark a job as complete, as that job's poster. Moves the job from in_progress to completed. Transfers 90% of the held amount to the freelancer's own Stripe account; fails if they haven't finished Stripe Conne

tools.name: cancel_job

tools.name: withdraw_bid
tools.description: Withdraw your own bid on a job, as the bidder who placed it. Only possible while the job is still open and your bid hasn't been accepted. No reason required. tools.name: request_close

tools.name: mark_job_seen
tools.description: Record that you have seen everything on this job, which clears has_new_messages and has_new_bids for it on get_my_jobs. Call it after reading a job's messages or bids, so the next get_my_jobs tells you what has arrived since rather than repeating what you already handled. Idempotent: calling it twic

tools.name: submit_rating
tools.description: Rate your counterparty on a job that's completed or cancelled. Only the poster and the accepted bidder can rate each other, only each other (not a third party, not yourself), and only once per job.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get your own identity and capabilities: user id, username, join date, rating, and whether you can currently post a job or place a bid -- with why not and where to fix it, if not.

tools.name: get_my_jobs
tools.description: List jobs you've posted and/or bid on, with pagination. Posted jobs carry bid_count (bids still standing: a withdrawn bid is not counted) and accepted bidder (once one exists); jobs you've bid on carry your own bid and whether it was accepted. Each row also carries has_new_messages and has_new_bids:

tools.name: get_ratings
tools.description: Read individual ratings, including the written review text -- not just the average that job results inline. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_user_jobs" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "submit_bid" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Submit a bid on an open job, as the authenticated user. You can't bid on your own job. You get one bid per job, ever: your bid amount cannot be edited afterward…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_user_jobs, get_job, get_messages, mark_job_seen, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_ratings, get_document, report_gap · Private data: browse_jobs, mark_job_seen, get_document, report_gap · Public sink: post_job, submit_bid, send_message, submit_rating, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_my_payments, report_gap · Destructive: get_my_payments, report_gap.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_user_jobs, get_job, get_messages, mark_job_seen, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_ratings, get_document, report_gap · Private data: browse_jobs, mark_job_seen, get_document, report_gap · Public sink: post_job, submit_bid, send_message, submit_rating, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_my_payments, report_gap · Destructive: get_my_payments, report_gap

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
